newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU postal notice tied to directive.
newsitem.headline: EU postal notice tied to directive.

text.p: Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Thursday a long-awaited notice on how competition rules will be applied to postal services will be published at the same time a directive on the sector is adopted.
"We think it's probably better to do it at the same time," he told a news conference.
That will disappoint private express mail operators and others who compete with state post offices and were hoping for speedy publication of the notice.
The Council formally adopted in April a common position on the postal services directive, COM(95)227, which sets out a timetable for opening the sector to competition.
It must now be approved by the European Parliament, which has co-decision powers over the text. Then it will go back to the Council for final adoption.

The Commission has promised a separate notice to spell out exactly how the Commission will enforce EU competition law in the postal sector, publishing a draft text in 1995. But it has delayed formal publication several times.

Private companies are especially interested in how the Commission will treat "cross-subsidies" -- the use by post offices of revenues from their monopoly services to subsidise those where they face competition.
But the notice is unpopular with the European Parliament, which does not like the fact that it would be issued unilaterally by the Commission.
The draft directive postpones significant postal liberalisation until at least January 1, 2003. It set that as a target date for opening direct mail and cross-border mail to competition.
